heroLead: Ontology Atlas is an open-source app that keeps what your code builds, and why, as Markdown in your repository. Claude Code and Codex read the same folder over MCP, and after a commit the map marks the concepts to recheck.

loop.title: Your agent reads it, a commit marks it, you allow it
loop.sub: The map is Markdown in your repository, so the same folder works at three moments.

read.title: Your agent reads the map before the code
read.body: Claude Code and Codex ask the folder over MCP what a concept is, what it contains and depends on, and which file holds it.

mark.title: After a commit, the concepts to recheck are marked
mark.body: Each concept names the file it describes. When a commit changes that file after the concept was last written, the map marks the concept in amber.
mark.commit: Your agent's commit · {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} changed

allow.title: Nothing is written until you allow it
allow.body: In the app's chat, an agent's change to the map waits as a card. Allow it once or deny it. What gets written is Markdown in the folder, never your code.

loop.note: The concept and file names are from this repository's own ontology. The commit and the proposal are examples.

start.title: Three steps to your own map

step1.title: Open your project's folder
step1.body: Atlas reads the Markdown already there, or starts an atlas/ folder in your repository, and shows the path before it writes anything.

step2.title: Let your agent draft the map
step2.body: The first card offers to have your coding agent read the code and propose the concepts it finds. Nothing is written until you allow it.

step3.title: Connect the agent you code with
step3.body: In {agents} › {mcp}, press {connect} for Claude Code or Codex and restart it. From then on it reads the same folder while it works.

screens.title: One folder, read on every screen
screens.sub: The same Markdown folder opens as a screen for each job in the app. Press a name to see that screen; Map opens live in this browser.
screens.mapLink: Map, opens the live map in this browser
screens.alt: The {name} screen of the Atlas app

source.title: Every line is public
source.sub: The app, the MCP server and the CLI sit in one repository. Read it, build it yourself, send a fix.

free.title: Free, and yours to change
free.body: The license is MIT. Use it on a company repository, fork it, or build the app from source.

local.title: No account and no Atlas backend
local.body: There is no sign-in and no backend run by Atlas. The map is read and written in a folder on your computer. A coding agent you connect talks to its own provider separately.

files.title: The record is plain Markdown
files.body: One concept is one .md file, kept in your own Git repository. Delete the app and the files stay.

together.title: Build it with us
together.body: Bugs and ideas arrive as issues, fixes as pull requests.

source.invite: If it was useful, a star helps the next person find it.

closingTitle: Ready to open your own folder?

tools.label: MCP tools
tools.body: An agent calls them to read the map and propose a change.

concepts.label: concepts
concepts.body: Atlas maps its own code too, in this repository's docs/ontology/.

relations.label: relations
relations.body: Between those concepts, written as names in the info block at the top of each file.

1.title: Your ontology is plain Markdown
1.body: Each concept is one .md file in the repository, read by people and agents alike.

2.title: The first lines are the graph
2.body: domain says where a concept belongs, kind what it is, dependencies what it relies on. Those lines become the map's points and lines.

3.title: Each file finds its place
3.body: Every concept settles beside the concept that holds it.

4.title: Relations draw themselves
4.body: The {relations} relations written in those files become the lines between them.

5.title: One map, read by you and your agents
5.body: This is this repository's real map: {concepts} concepts and {relations} relations.

1.title: What your agent reads first
1.body: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and rule files: everything an agent reads before a task, on one screen.

2.title: What stops it before it acts
2.body: Hooks block irreversible commands before they run. See which hook stops what.

3.title: What checks its work
3.body: Type checks, lint and tests: what verifies the work once the agent is done.
